h: לְרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ אֱלוּל, ג׳ Rosh Chodesh Elul, 3

p: "He made the letter yud king over action," and so on,
and the left hand in the soul."
The letter yud of the holy Name
indicates the sefirah of Chochmah, wisdom.
You made them all with wisdom;
the earth is full of Your possessions."
that is, all the works of Hashem, blessed be He,
were made through the attribute of wisdom.
For first, at the creation of light,
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב,
"And Elokim saw the light, that it was good,"
and afterward, throughout the works of Creation,
it is written at every utterance:
"And Elokim saw that it was good."
and it is written (Mishlei 6:23): "And Torah is light."
So in every work of Creation
רָאָה אֱלֹהִים כִּי יֵשׁ בּוֹ אוֹר,
Elokim saw that there was light in it,
and this is what is written: "that it was good."
"The earth is full of Your possessions":
אוֹמְרִים בְּשֵׁם הָרַבִּי רַבִּי בּוּנִם זַצַ״ל
they say in the name of the Rebbe, Reb Bunim, zt"l,
that the entire world is full
only in order to acquire You.
That is, in all of creation
there are words of Torah to learn from it,
as we find that Avraham Avinu
and from where did he learn the Torah?
He learned it only from all of creation,
which is full of words of Torah.
It is similar to what they said (Eruvin 100b):
we would have learned modesty from the cat
and honesty from the ant," and so on.
And it is written (Devarim 28:9): "And you shall walk in His ways,"
for all the mitzvos are the ways
of the Holy One, blessed be He,
which He emanated for the conduct of the world,
and He Himself fulfills the mitzvos first
and Yisrael were commanded to learn from this
So too must a person have
כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו עַל פִּי חָכְמָה וְתוֹרָה.
all his deeds be according to wisdom and Torah.
וְיַד שְׂמֹאל שֶׁהוּא מוֹרֶה עַל יִרְאָה,
are the aspects of Chesed and Gevurah
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶתַח אֵלִיָּהוּ, תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר יז, א),
(as they said in Pasach Eliyahu, Tikkunei Zohar 17a),
and they are the attributes of Avraham and Yitzchak,
the aspects of love and fear.
and he was zealous in the positive mitzvos,
קְרָא זְרִיזוּתֵיהּ דְּאַבְרָהָם קָא מַשְׁמַע לָן.
"The verse comes to teach us Avraham's zeal."
His whole occupation was to bring the entire world
under the wings of the Shechinah,
"and he called there in the Name of Hashem," etc.;
the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, to be called
by the mouth of every passerby;
וּבְמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (לֶךְ לְךָ, בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה לט, יד)
and in the Midrash Rabbah (Lech Lecha, Bereishis Rabbah 39:14)
that he would convert the men.
Although after his passing they returned to their old ways,
nevertheless, all the days of his life
they held fast to the way of Hashem,
וְהָיָה לוֹ מְכוּוָּן לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם בָּזֶה.
and his intent in this was for the sake of Heaven.
This corresponds to the right hand,
"the right hand, which is extended in mitzvos";
and it corresponds to the positive mitzvos,
which stem from the attribute of love.
And Yitzchak corresponds to the left arm,
which is the attribute of fear and restraint.
Therefore we do not find regarding Yitzchak
and where have we heard?" and so on —
"'the dwellings of his father' — the conversions of his father."
except one in whom he recognized
that there was truly a good spark
and who would remain within Yisrael,
since his attribute was restraint and fear,
and he saw that the dross, which is Esav,
performs a deed that is strange,
אַף שֶׁהָיָה שְׁמוֹ מוֹרֶה עַל מַעֲשָׂיו לְטוֹבָה,
even though his name pointed to his deeds favorably,
"Esav — he does the will of his Maker."
וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד יַד שְׂמֹאל, יָד כֵּהָה,
This corresponds to the left hand, the weaker hand;
and in the Midrash (Tanchuma there) it says:
"the left hand, which is not extended in mitzvos";
And this is the meaning of "the left hand in the soul":
the deeds of the left hand
צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת גַּם כֵּן בְּמִדַּת חָכְמָה.
must also be in the attribute of wisdom.
And with this the month of Elul was created,
for on Rosh Chodesh there ascended
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
and this was on the first day of Rosh Chodesh.
דְּמִטַּעַם זֶה כָּתְבוּ הָרַשַׁ״ל (חָכְמַת שְׁלֹמֹה שַׁבָּת פח, א)
For this reason the Rashal (Chochmas Shlomo, Shabbos 88a)
and the Shelah (Maseches Rosh Hashanah, Ner Mitzvah) wrote
to begin blowing the shofar on the first day of Rosh Chodesh;
but the custom is not so.
"And with the second Tablets I am giving you
that there be in them Midrash, halachos and aggados;
this is what is written," and so on:
This means that after the downfall
in order to rectify the abundant anger,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, showed Moshe
the fine points of the Torah and the fine points of the Sofrim,
and what the Sofrim would one day innovate.
This was with the second Tablets;
for with the first, had they not been broken,
there would have been no need for innovation at all,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד, דִּכְתִיב (יִרְמְיָה לא, לג)
just as it will be in the future, as it is written (Yirmiyah 31:33):
וְלֹא יְלַמְּדוּ עוֹד אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ וְגוֹמֵר
"And they shall no longer teach each man his fellow," etc.,
from the least of them to the greatest of them."
And so too at the first Commandments,
the learning of Torah was implanted in their hearts
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים א, ב).
(as is written in Midrash Rabbah, Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2).
they would have been given only
the five books of the Torah," and so on.
For at the time of the Giving of the Torah
they put "we will do" before "we will hear,"
were solely according to the will of Hashem, blessed be He;
and had the downfall not occurred,
it would have remained so always,
since the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts
at the moment they heard the utterance
(as is written in the Midrash Rabbah cited above).
you will rectify "we will do" as well;
that is, through the abundant wisdom
they will be able to rectify the abundant anger.
Therefore the month of Elul was created
with the letter yud and with action,
so that it be according to wisdom,
And this is the meaning of
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ הַפֵּירוּשׁ בַּפָּסוּק (דְּבָרִים ל, יד)
As we have explained the verse (Devarim 30:14):
"In your mouth and in your heart, to do it" —
it does not say "and in your deeds,"
because the main thing on man's part
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קס, א)
as stated in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 160a):
לָא בָּעֵי מִינָּן אֶלָּא לִבָּא וְכוּלֵּי,
wants nothing from us but the heart," and so on;
"The Holy One, blessed be He, wants the heart."
Therefore it says "in your mouth and in your heart":
through the words of Torah in your mouth —
עַל יְדֵי זֶה יִהְיֶה נִכְנָס לַלֵּב,
by means of this they will enter the heart,
and that is "and in your heart";
Hashem, blessed be He, will help.
his intention should be to do,
וְאָז יַעֲזוֹר לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לִגְמוֹר,
and then Hashem, blessed be He, will help him complete it;
therefore it does not say "and in your deeds."
"The Merciful One said: Rest on the Shabbos day
just as I rested on it."
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהוּזְהֲרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל הַשַּׁבָּת
And wherever Yisrael were warned about Shabbos,
"Six days you shall work" or "you shall do";
meaning that they were enjoined to do,
אַךְ שֶׁהַמַּעֲשֶׂה יִהְיֶה עַל פִּי הַחָכְמָה
but that the doing be according to wisdom,
as was the work of the days of Creation,
and the main toil is the toil of Torah
שֶׁהֲרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחָאי וַחֲבֵירָיו
for indeed Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and his colleagues
לֹא הָיוּ מַפְסִיקִין אֲפִילּוּ לִתְפִלָּה (שַׁבָּת יא, א).
would not interrupt even for prayer (Shabbos 11a),
would pray only from thirty days
for prayer is the toil of speech.
כָּל שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים
any that can be done by others,
rather, the main thing is the toil of Torah.
And this too is called action,
for the movement of one's lips counts as an action.
is teshuvah and good deeds," and so on,
'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem.'"
And teshuvah is the aspect of fear of Hashem,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְרָשׁ בַּגְּמָרָא (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יט, א)
as expounded in the Gemara (Avodah Zarah 19a):
"'Fortunate is the man who fears Hashem' —
fortunate is he who does teshuvah
while he is still a man."
For through the fear of Hashem,
which comes by picturing before oneself
that the King of kings of kings,
the Holy One, blessed be He, stands over him
against His will, blessed be His Name.
"Good understanding to all who do them";
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ה, א) אֵין טוֹב אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה.
as they said (Berachos 5a): "'Good' means nothing other than Torah."
according to the reading printed in the margin:
"It does not say 'to those who learn them'
to those who act for its own sake,
and not to those who act not for its own sake."
that it means those who act for its own sake?
רַק הַפֵּירוּשׁ עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין צט, ב)
Rather, it is explained by what they said in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 99b):
"It is as though he made the words of Torah,
'And you shall keep the words of this covenant
That is, he expounded it as though it were written
וְכֵן אִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קיג, א),
and so it is stated in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 113a),
that one should make the Good.
And this is the meaning of "le'oseihem":
those who make the words of Torah;
and this is only when they act for its own sake —
אָז הוּא כְּאִלּוּ עֲשָׂאוֹ לְהַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
then it is as though he made the words of Torah.
And this is "good understanding to all who do them":
And this is "He made the letter yud king over action":
that action be according to wisdom.
And this is the preparation in the month of Elul,
for in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed
דִּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ שֶׁבְּתִשְׁרֵי נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה י, ב),
who holds that the world was created in Tishrei (Rosh Hashanah 10b),
אִם יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין תְּשׁוּבָה נִגְאָלִין (סַנְהֶדְרִין צז, ב).
"If Yisrael do teshuvah, they are redeemed" (Sanhedrin 97b).
And even Rabbi Yehoshua agrees with this;
דְּאַף אִם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּשׁוּבָה
that even if, Heaven forbid, they do not do teshuvah,
"And not with money" — not with teshuvah, and so on.
that they are destined to be redeemed in Nissan,
which is a month of mercy,
as was the redemption from Egypt,
even though they were sunk there.
they are destined to be redeemed in Tishrei.
And for this the month of Elul was created
with the letter yud, over action:
so that it be with wisdom,
which is the utterance "Let there be light,"
corresponding to the five books of the Torah."
And it is stated (in the Midrash there, 3:1):
"The opening of Your words gives light" (Tehillim 119:130) —
"from the opening of Your mouth there was light for us."
And the first letter of this utterance
and afterward, throughout the works of Creation,
it is written "that it was good,"
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם אוֹר כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
meaning that there is light in them, as mentioned above.
And all the works of Creation,
except for the creation of man,
took place in the month of Elul according to Rabbi Eliezer.
And these and these are the words of the living G-d,
for in Tishrei it arose in thought to be created
(תּוֹסָפוֹת רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כז, א ד״ה כְּמַאן),
and in the whole passage of the utterances of Creation,
which was according to the thought
to be created with the attribute of judgment,
only the Name Elokim is mentioned,
where He joined in the attribute of mercy.
the world was created on the twenty-fifth of Elul,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּפְּסִיקְתָּא (פְּסִיקְתָּא דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא כג, א).
as is written in the Pesikta (Pesikta DeRav Kahana 23:1).
Therefore it says in Sefer Yetzirah:
"He made the letter yud king over action
And it is known that it is called Rosh Chodesh,
and not "the beginning of the month,"
because it is the head of the month,
וְגוּפָא בָּתַר רֵישָׁא אָזִיל (עֵירוּבִין מא, א).
and the body follows the head (Eruvin 41a).
includes all the holiness of the month;
and in this month took place the main work of Creation,
and "You made them all with wisdom."
"And the left hand in the soul":
after the month of Elul is given
so that it be according to wisdom,
then it will be according to the original thought,
אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כט).
And Tishrei accords with the thought;
אָז בְּתִשְׁרֵי עֲתִידִין לְהִגָּאֵל (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יא, א),
then in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed (Rosh Hashanah 11a),
after everything is rectified on Yom Kippur,
and it becomes clear that in all the deeds
which proceed in order from the six days of Creation,
they shall become white as snow" (Shabbos 89b);
דְּנָפִיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א לב, א),
that emerges from within darkness (Zohar I 32a),
and then they will be redeemed.
חָשַׁב חוֹדֶשׁ אֱלוּל כְּנֶגֶד שֵׁבֶט גָּד.
matched the month of Elul with the tribe of Gad.
וְהוּא עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה עא, ט)
This is based on what they said (Bereishis Rabbah 71:9):
there has come the one who is destined to cut down
the foundation of the nations of the world;
שֶׁהוּא יְגַלֶּה כָּל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
for he will reveal all of the Torah she'b'al peh
that can be revealed in this world,
"This passage Eliyahu is destined to expound."
"the Tishbi will resolve difficulties and questions."
And as for why it says specifically Eliyahu —
even though Mashiach comes from the tribe of Yehudah,
וְדָוִד גַּם כֵּן מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת,
and David too is a chariot for the attribute of Malchus
וְהָיָה רַבָּן שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
and was the master of those who possess ruach hakodesh,
the root of Torah she'b'al peh —
but with all of them, they are are not present in every generation,
which is not so with Eliyahu;
שֶׁאִלּוּ לֹא חָטָא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן וְכוּלֵּי
that had Adam HaRishon not sinned," and so on,
"he would have lived and endured forever,
there already was Eliyahu, who did not sin,
and he lives and endures forever."
וְאַף דְּגַם בְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And although regarding Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, too,
וְכֵן בְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ אִיתָא (סוֹטָה יג, ב)
and likewise regarding Moshe Rabbeinu it is stated (Sotah 13b):
אַף עַל פִּי כֵן לֹא נִזְכַּר מֵהֶם;
"Was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized?" and so on;
the language of burial is written (Devarim 34:6).
This is not so with Eliyahu,
שֶׁאֱלִישָׁע רָאָה כְּשֶׁעָלָה לַשָּׁמַיִם (מְלָכִים ב ב, יב),
for Elisha saw him when he went up to Heaven (II Melachim 2:12);
וְכֵן הוּא עוֹמֵד וּמִתְגַּלֶּה בְּכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת
and so he stands and reveals himself in every generation
to whoever is worthy of it,
for he lives and endures forever.
וְכֵן נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם זֶה גָּד,
And so the tribe was named Gad on this account,
for from him comes the one who is destined to cut down
the foundation of the nations of the world,
and he lives and endures in every generation.
וְהַחוֹדֶשׁ זֶה הוּא כְּנֶגֶד נֶפֶשׁ זֶה,
And this month corresponds to this soul,
for it is the preparation to rectify the "we will do"
שֶׁבּוֹ נִיתַּן לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
in which Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, was given
together with the Torah she'b'al peh,
and this is the preparation for the month of Tishrei,
in which they are destined to be redeemed, as stated.
And because of this, this month is reckoned
as corresponding to the tribe of Gad:
"there has come the one destined to cut down," and so on,
שֶׁהוּא יְגַלֶּה כָּל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
who will reveal all of the Torah she'b'al peh
that can be revealed in this world;
and through him they will draw out all the life
that is found among the nations of the world;
and then the rectification will be complete,
and then they will be redeemed.
